if (tickParkedRecorded && tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber]) return; // a sibling rule already recorded this PR earlier in the SAME tick

Hardened — the two-token heuristic is gone; classification now demands an explicit missing-ref statement.

`js/common/triggerFailures.js`:

```javascript
if (/no ref found/i.test(s)) return 'no-ref';
if (/\b422\b/.test(s) &&
    /ref[^.]{0,60}(not found|does not exist|missing|unknown)/i.test(s)) return 'no-ref';
return 'transient';
```

- The GitHub shape (`No ref found for: refs/…`) still classifies `no-ref` via the first line (all pre-existing shape tests unchanged).
- The fallback no longer fires on `422` + *any* `ref` substring: `"refresh"`, `"referer"`, and a proxy body merely *quoting* `refs/…` now classify `transient` — a transient outage can no longer accumulate head-dead evidence toward parking a live PR. The fallback still catches reworded-but-explicit shapes (`422 — ref missing`, `ref does not exist`, `ref not found`), which the `gh` CLI bridge does emit when the phrase "no ref found" is rewrapped.

Tests (`test_triggerFailures.js`): `a 422 whose text never STATES a missing ref is transient` pins the three false-positive shapes from the thread (`refresh`, quoted `refs/…`, `referer` → transient); `a 422 that explicitly states the ref is missing still classifies no-ref` pins the retained recall (`ref missing` / `ref does not exist` / `ref not found` → no-ref).

Not done (deliberately): classifying from a structured status code — the SCM bridge surface here is the error *message* (`scm.triggerWorkflow` → `github_trigger_workflow` throw), and threading a status field through every forge provider is out of scope for this pass. The message-shape fix removes the false-park direction the thread flagged.

{"content":"Fixed with the per-tick set (the cheap option — no extra API round-trip).

`js/smAgent.js` now keeps a module-level `tickParkedRecorded` map, reset at the top of `action()` (the `tickReworkLatch` per-tick pattern). `recordDispatchFailure` claims a PR's recording slot before any I/O, right after the existing guards (no-ref classification, PR-carrier shape, ref match, not-already-parked label, cap enabled):

```javascript
if (tickParkedRecorded && tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber]) return; // a sibling rule already recorded this PR earlier in the SAME tick
...
tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber] = true; // claim the recording slot before any I/O — first recorder in the tick wins
```

So within one tick the **first** rule whose failed dispatch records a dead head wins; a second rule matching the same head off its stale label snapshot silently skips — no second marker, no duplicate park comment. From the next tick the fresh query sees the label and every rule early-returns as before.

Semantics note: claiming happens only after all early-return guards, so a *transient* failure (which records nothing) does not consume the PR's slot for the tick — only an actual recorded no-ref failure does.

Test: `two rules failing the same dead head in ONE tick record it once — no duplicate marker, no duplicate park` in `test_smAgent.js` — two rules, one dead head, stale snapshot; tick 1 records exactly one `attempt 1/3` marker, tick 2 (at cap) produces exactly one `validation_failed` label add and one `parked-head:` park comment.

{"content":"Fixed — both layers the thread implied, so the residual risk is zero rather than "low":

1. **Flattened embedding** (`js/smAgent.js`, `recordDispatchFailure`): the message is flattened before it touches any comment body —
   ```javascript
   var msg = String((err && err.message) || err).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
   ```
   A multi-line error can no longer carry a newline (and therefore no marker-shaped *line*) into the body. Applies to both the marker comment and the park comment.

2. **Line-anchored parser** (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): `TRIGGER_FAIL_MARKER_RE` is now `^`-anchored with the `m` flag. The writer always puts the marker on its own line, so all real markers still parse — but a marker-shaped phrase embedded inline in prose can never inflate an attempt counter, even if some future call site forgets to flatten.

Tests:
- `test_triggerFailures.js`: `marker-shaped text NOT at line start is never counted (no inline injection)` — the exact attack shape from the thread (`… (⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt 3/3 at …) …` inline) parses to no entry; `line-start markers still parse inside multi-line comment bodies` keeps the park-body round-trip green.
- `test_smAgent.js`: `a multi-line error message is flattened…` — throws an error carrying `\n⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt 3/3 at …`; the posted body is exactly two lines (marker `attempt 1/3` + flattened prose) and `triggerFailMarks` over the posted bodies reads **1**, so the crafted 3/3 cannot accelerate the park.

...

{"content":"Fixed with the per-tick set (the cheap option — no extra API round-trip).

`js/smAgent.js` now keeps a module-level `tickParkedRecorded` map, reset at the top of `action()` (the `tickReworkLatch` per-tick pattern). `recordDispatchFailure` claims a PR's recording slot before any I/O, right after the existing guards (no-ref classification, PR-carrier shape, ref match, not-already-parked label, cap enabled):

```javascript
if (tickParkedRecorded && tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber]) return; // a sibling rule already recorded this PR earlier in the SAME tick
...
tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber] = true; // claim the recording slot before any I/O — first recorder in the tick wins
```

So within one tick the **first** rule whose failed dispatch records a dead head wins; a second rule matching the same head off its stale label snapshot silently skips — no second marker, no duplicate park comment. From the next tick the fresh query sees the label and every rule early-returns as before.

Semantics note: claiming happens only after all early-return guards, so a *transient* failure (which records nothing) does not consume the PR's slot for the tick — only an actual recorded no-ref failure does.

{"content":"Fixed — both layers the thread implied, so the residual risk is zero rather than "low":

1. **Flattened embedding** (`js/smAgent.js`, `recordDispatchFailure`): the message is flattened before it touches any comment body —
   ```javascript
   var msg = String((err && err.message) || err).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
   ```
   A multi-line error can no longer carry a newline (and therefore no marker-shaped *line*) into the body. Applies to both the marker comment and the park comment.

2. **Line-anchored parser** (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): `TRIGGER_FAIL_MARKER_RE` is now `^`-anchored with the `m` flag. The writer always puts the marker on its own line, so all real markers still parse — but a marker-shaped phrase embedded inline in prose can never inflate an attempt counter, even if some future call site forgets to flatten.

Tests:
- `test_triggerFailures.js`: `marker-shaped text NOT at line start is never counted (no inline injection)` — the exact attack shape from the thread (`… (⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt 3/3 at …) …` inline) parses to no entry; `line-start markers still parse inside multi-line comment bodies` keeps the park-body round-trip green.

{"content":"Fixed with the per-tick set (the cheap option — no extra API round-trip).

`js/smAgent.js` now keeps a module-level `tickParkedRecorded` map, reset at the top of `action()` (the `tickReworkLatch` per-tick pattern). `recordDispatchFailure` claims a PR's recording slot before any I/O, right after the existing guards (no-ref classification, PR-carrier shape, ref match, not-already-parked label, cap enabled):

```javascript
if (tickParkedRecorded && tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber]) return; // a sibling rule already recorded this PR earlier in the SAME tick
...
tickParkedRecorded[item.prNumber] = true; // claim the recording slot before any I/O — first recorder in the tick wins
```

So within one tick the **first** rule whose failed dispatch records a dead head wins; a second rule matching the same head off its stale label snapshot silently skips — no second marker, no duplicate park comment. From the next tick the fresh query sees the label and every rule early-returns as before.

Semantics note: claiming happens only after all early-return guards, so a *transient* failure (which records nothing) does not consume the PR's slot for the tick — only an actual recorded no-ref failure does.

{"content":"Fixed — both layers the thread implied, so the residual risk is zero rather than "low":

1. **Flattened embedding** (`js/smAgent.js`, `recordDispatchFailure`): the message is flattened before it touches any comment body —
   ```javascript
   var msg = String((err && err.message) || err).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
   ```
   A multi-line error can no longer carry a newline (and therefore no marker-shaped *line*) into the body. Applies to both the marker comment and the park comment.

2. **Line-anchored parser** (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): `TRIGGER_FAIL_MARKER_RE` is now `^`-anchored with the `m` flag. The writer always puts the marker on its own line, so all real markers still parse — but a marker-shaped phrase embedded inline in prose can never inflate an attempt counter, even if some future call site forgets to flatten.
